title: Blocks and object boundaries
summary: Use reduce with a block, then review an error handler that swallows failures.

scenario.briefing: A campus totals service needs a block-based reduction and a narrower rescue.

objectives.description: Apply the taught syntax in a working file.
Review an artifact and identify the concrete risks.

hints: The block receives the accumulator and the current value.
Return sum + value from the block.

misconceptions.description: Expecting each to return the accumulated value.
misconceptions.testDescription: The collection is reduced with an explicit seed and block.
misconceptions.feedback: each returns the original collection. Use reduce or inject when you need an accumulated result.

misconceptions.description: Reducing without a seed on an empty collection.
misconceptions.diagnostic: Calling values.reduce { |sum, value| sum + value } without 0, so empty input returns nil.
misconceptions.feedback: Without a seed, reduce uses the first element as the initial accumulator and returns nil for an empty collection. Pass 0 when zero is the correct empty result.

misconceptions.description: Using rescue without an exception class.
misconceptions.feedback: A bare rescue catches StandardError, including mistakes you wanted to see. Name the exception you can handle.

misconceptions.description: Accepting a silent zero as a safe fallback.
misconceptions.feedback: Returning zero for malformed input hides the failure from the caller. Report or raise, and narrow the rescue class.

sections.title: Blocks carry behavior
sections.body: Methods such as reduce receive a block and call it with accumulated state. The block's return value becomes the next accumulator, and the seed gives an empty collection a defined result.

sections.title: Objects and modules
sections.body: Classes define object state and behavior. Modules group reusable behavior and can be included into classes, which keeps shared logic out of a single inheritance chain.

sections.title: Tooling around the code
sections.body: Bundler installs the gems a project declares in its Gemfile. Minitest and RSpec describe behavior as tests, and RuboCop reports style and consistency problems before review.

vocabulary.definition: A method that combines a collection into a single accumulated value.
A namespace and mixin unit for shared behavior.

steps.title: Review the rescue
steps.prompt: Review the error handler and select every real problem.
hints: Look at what the rescue clause actually catches.
A broad rescue also catches programming mistakes.
The caller cannot tell invalid text from a real zero.

artifact.title: parse_count.rb
artifact.caption: The rescue swallows every failure and reports zero.

findings.label: The bare rescue catches every StandardError.
Returning zero hides malformed input from the caller.
The handler should rescue ArgumentError for invalid text.
The handler is safe because zero is always a valid count.

verdicts.label: Block until the rescue is narrowed and the failure is visible.
Ship it; returning zero is acceptable.

steps.explanation: A bare rescue catches unrelated programming errors. Rescue ArgumentError and decide explicitly whether to return nil, raise, or report the invalid input.
